en: Does the underlying tendency to sensual lust arise in one in whom the underlying tendency to aversion arises? Yes.
Or rather, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust arise in one in whom the underlying tendency to aversion arises? Yes.
Does the underlying tendency to conceit arise in one in whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust arises? Yes.
Or, when the underlying tendency to conceit arises in someone, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust arise in that person?

In the case of a non-returner (*anāgāmī*), the underlying tendency to conceit arises, but the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not arise in him. In three types of persons, both the underlying tendency to conceit and the underlying tendency to sensual lust arise (this should be expanded).
When the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not arise in someone, does the underlying tendency to aversion (*paṭighānusaya*) not arise in that person? Yes.
Or again, for whom the underlying tendency to aversion does not arise, for that person does the underlying tendency to sensual lust not arise? Yes.
For whom the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not arise, for that person does the underlying tendency to conceit not arise?

In the case of a non-returner, the underlying tendency to sensual lust does not arise, but the underlying tendency to conceit does not necessarily not arise. In the case of an arahant, neither the underlying tendency to sensual lust nor the underlying tendency to conceit arises.
Or again, for one in whom the underlying tendency to conceit does not arise, does the underlying tendency to sensual lust not arise? Yes. (This should be expanded in detail.
